name: Daily Shorts factory
what: 5 gated 61-72 s videos a day, six series, banked ahead
note: Exists. The atom every other rail is cut from.

name: Variety layer: motion cards + Flow/Veo hook clips
what: Animated number/chart cards (live) and 3 owner-made Flow clips a day for hook beats; per-series caption/voice variants
metric: avg view-through of card videos vs still-only
note: Fixes the 'one-dimensional' problem and the YouTube inauthentic-content risk at the same time.

name: Weekly long-form: 'Money Rules Weekly' (8-10 min, 16:9, chapters)
what: Seven best Shorts re-cut into one landscape episode with intro card and chapters
metric: watch hours per episode; RPM vs Shorts
note: Long-form monetizes far better than Shorts and counts toward watch-hours eligibility.

name: Audio edition: daily 60 s + weekly podcast episode
what: voice.wav + music already exist per video; compile a weekly audio episode for a free podcast host

name: Repurposing kit per video (thread, carousel, pin, newsletter item, LinkedIn post, audio)
what: Every video also emits five or six text/image assets, no LLM cost
metric: assets produced per video; clicks per asset once posted
note: The printing press: one atom, many surfaces.
built: faceless/repurpose.py: thread, LinkedIn, carousel, pin, newsletter item, audio; runs after every publish

name: Money Rules Library website + calculators (SEO/AEO)
what: One citable page per video, schema.org, llms.txt, calculators
metric: indexed pages; AI-assistant mention rate (weekly probe)

name: Newsletter: Quiet Money Weekly (auto-compiled issue)
what: Weekly issue assembled from the week's kits; list is the asset that every product sells into
note: Products convert 10-50x better to a list than to a view.
built: faceless/repurpose.weekly_issue: compiles the week into channel/newsletter/; marked NOT SENDABLE until postal address + unsubscribe exist

name: Money Reset 7-day challenge as an autoresponder
what: Turn the existing checklist into 7 emails: the welcome sequence and first product pitch
built: faceless/autoresponder.py + channel/offers/autoresponder: welcome + 7 daily emails, every number computed by moneymath, rule-checked (length, banned phrases, footer merge tags); import-ready sequence.json

name: Debt Payoff & Compound Interest Planner (spreadsheet)
what: Real formulas: card payoff vs snowball vs avalanche, compound growth, what-if; built from our moneymath.py
note: Built entirely by the agent; Gumroad takes 10% and has no AI rule; Etsy needs the AI disclosure line.
built: channel/products/debt-payoff-planner: avalanche/snowball engine with rolled-over minimums, minimums-only baseline, compound table, pay-or-invest check; recalculated in LibreOffice for both methods and matched to an independent simulation

name: Rat Race Escape Planner (passive-income calculator + side-income tracker)
what: 4% rule target, years-to-freedom, side income log, leverage what-ifs; ties to the Escape the Rat Race series
built: channel/products/rat-race-escape-planner: 6-tab workbook recalculated in LibreOffice and matched to Python math; listing + 5 real previews

name: Printable budget pack (50/30/20, sinking funds, subscription audit, net worth)
what: Branded PDFs/PNGs from our brand kit and fonts; sold as a pack and as the Money Reset Kit bundle with P1+P2
note: Printables are crowded; the bundle with real calculators is the difference.
built: faceless/product_print.py + channel/products/money-reset-printables: six pen-and-paper pages (paycheck split, subscription audit, sinking funds, debt list, net worth), Letter and A4 PDFs, margin-safety check, listing

name: Money Reset Kit bundle (P1+P2+P3)
what: Anchor offer: one price, instant delivery, upsell from the free checklist
built: channel/products/money-reset-kit: zip of both planners + printables with read-me and licence; bundle listing with test prices marked as assumptions

name: Original 'money rules' typography posters (print on demand)
what: Our own text art, not copies of best-sellers, through Printify to Etsy
note: Low margin and crowded; test small. Etsy requires the AI-assistance disclosure line.

name: Fiverr: productized faceless-channel brand kit
what: Name + colors + niche in, 60 s later: avatar, banner, watermark, OG card, logo SVG (our brand.py), then owner-curated concept variants
note: Reuses machinery we already own and a marketplace that already sends traffic.
built: faceless/brandkit.py + channel/services/brand-kit: avatar, banner (text proven inside the mobile-safe area), watermark, share image, favicons, logo, palette, BRAND.md; 4 labeled gallery samples; GIG.md with tiers, exact promises and what not to promise

name: Fiverr studio mode: concept sheets in minutes for logo/art/character gigs
what: Generate 6-12 directions per brief with our image stack; owner picks and refines; faster turnaround is the edge

name: Adobe Stock AI: abstract backgrounds, textures, objects (no people, brands, artist names)
what: Volume pipeline from our image stack, labeled 'Created using generative AI tools'
note: Crowded and low per-asset income; test 100 assets before any scale. Confirm Cloudflare/FLUX terms allow commercial resale first.

name: YouTube Partner Program + TikTok Creator Rewards
what: Eligibility gates: 1,000 subs plus watch hours or Shorts views; 10k followers for TikTok; keep AI labels on
note: Slow; the scanner already flags TikTok's 'minimal original input' risk.

name: Finance affiliates + sponsors (with disclosure)
what: Savings, budgeting, investing apps, only after an audience exists; every post carries the disclosure
note: Highest-regulation corner of the niche; promised returns are banned by our own rules.

name: Identity layer: one owner-controlled domain mailbox with plus-addresses per platform
what: ops+youtube@, ops+gumroad@, etc. forwarded into one inbox the agent can read through Composio Gmail
note: Cheaper and less likely to trip bot detection than agent-created inboxes.

name: Metrics loop: YouTube via Composio, others pasted weekly
what: Feeds pillar weights, this ranking, and the forecast with real numbers
note: Every score here is a guess until this exists. Windsor.ai (free plan) can read TikTok Organic once the Quiet Money account is connected; its only connected account today is another channel's, so we do not read it.

name: Flow lane: daily shot list in, owner's clips back, renderer uses them
what: We write the 3 best prompts for tomorrow's hook/payoff beats; owner generates in Flow (free 50 credits) and drops the files; the renderer picks them up
metric: share of videos with a real clip; retention lift
kill: owner stops dropping clips (then it's just a prompt file)
note: Compliant with Flow's terms; the unofficial automations are blocked below. The automatic Muapi route (O12) can do the same job without the owner's ten minutes.
built: faceless/flow.py: daily 3-prompt shot list, inbox, hook-clip claim, renderer cut with still fallback

name: Clone best-selling Etsy designs with agents (the StarNet pitch)
what: Find top sellers, generate near-copies, auto-list on Etsy/Printify
note: Copying others' designs is an IP and Etsy-originality problem; StarNet's README never mentions this workflow, only the promo video does.

name: Reverse-engineered Flow automation (gflow-cli) with a saved Google login
what: Headless browser using the owner's Google session cookies to spend free credits
note: Unofficial endpoints plus session credentials: ban risk on the Google account the owner uses daily, and brittle. The compliant Flow lane (O4) gets most of the benefit.

name: Agents that create and operate platform accounts (AgentMail inboxes + signups)
what: Run `agentid-cli init`, sign agents up to platforms with their own inboxes
note: Platforms ban automated signups and demand phone/ID; account creation stays with the owner. AgentMail/Goshen are only for a support inbox later.

name: Prompt packs as products on Etsy
what: Sell lists of prompts
note: Verified 2026-10-08 on Etsy's own AI stance page: it prohibits selling AI prompt bundles (and its Creativity Standards list them as not allowed).

name: Go live: channel accounts + auto-posting (Upload-Post)
what: Create the three accounts (@quietmoneyrules), connect them, switch publish mode from local to upload_post
kill: n/a: the business does not exist without it
note: Everything else compounds on this. Account creation stays with the owner (platforms ban automated signups).

name: Semantic QA: Clef decision model gates every still and script
what: Typed yes/no probabilities for readable text, faces and logos in each still (flagged beats become designed cards), and for promised returns, product pushing and hype in each script
metric: share of stills flagged; videos held by a false positive
kill: false-positive holds on more than 5% of videos for 2 weeks
note: Apache-2.0 model on the Cloudflare key we already have; about 28 neurons a still against 417 to generate it. Calibrated on 40 cached stills and 30 scripts; positive controls (face 0.92, text 0.98) and a real calculator-keys still (0.77) all flagged; 0 false positives on the 30 published scripts.
built: faceless/providers/clef.py + faceless/qa.py, wired into visuals, the script loop and the gauntlet (no_faces, image_qa, no_promised_returns, no_specific_advice, no_hype); decide.py gets a clef backend

name: Music library: real instrumental beds per series (Lyria RealTime, free tier)
what: 12 distinct beds generated once and rotated by series and seed, replacing the one procedural bed that made every video sound alike
metric: music variety in the sameness audit; average view duration
kill: any copyright or Content ID claim on a bed, or no retention lift after 30 videos
note: Paid Lyria 3.x has no free tier (HTTP 429 on our key); the experimental RealTime model streams on the free tier. AI-generated music needs the YouTube AI label (we keep it on). Output is SynthID-watermarked.
built: faceless/musiclib.py + providers/music.py + assets/music; render picks a bed by series, compresses it and matches the old bed's loudness

name: Policy watchdog and verified platform rules
what: Weekly re-read of the 12 rule pages that govern us, with a diff of rule sentences; a dated digest of what each platform allows
metric: rule changes caught before they cost an account or a listing
note: Six pages are fetchable by plain HTTP; six need the weekly session's Exa fetch and `faceless policy --record` (the first record is the baseline). Found while verifying: Gumroad bans products that discuss credit improvement; YouTube's inauthentic-content rule names templated AI content.
built: faceless/policy.py + channel/compliance/watchlist.json + platform-rules.md; scout runs it and raises proposals

name: Variety audit and semantic duplicate gate
what: Sameness score for the last 20 videos (meaning, openers, formats, music, series mix) and a hold for a script that teaches what an earlier one already did
metric: sameness risk below 35; scripts held as duplicates
kill: the audit never moves a decision after 8 weeks
note: Embeddings (Gemini free tier, Cloudflare EmbeddingGemma as fallback) centered on our own history. Real finding: two 'the 10-year delay' videos on the same day (similarity 0.70), three 'frugal secretary' stories (0.62-0.66) and a start-early pair at 0.76. EmbeddingGemma 2 (Apache-2.0, 2026-10-06) is not hosted yet; the model name is one config line.
built: faceless/embed.py + variety.py + qa.duplicate_gates; scout raises a proposal at risk 60 or more

name: LongCat as a third script provider (free daily allowance)
what: Meituan's MIT-licensed LongCat models through an OpenAI-compatible API, used when Gemini's free tier is spent
metric: scripts served by LongCat when Gemini and OpenRouter are out
kill: quality below Gemini on the judge for 10 scripts
note: Provider is built and skipped without a key. LongCat-Image (Apache-2.0, 6B) and LongCat-Video (MIT, 13.6B) need GPUs: parked until a free hosted endpoint exists.
built: faceless/providers/llm.py longcat() in the chain after Gemini

name: Fillable PDF versions of the printable pack
what: Type-in fields on the six printable pages so buyers can use them on a tablet or screen
kill: no lift in conversion after 200 views
note: Digital planners that fill on a tablet are the common format on Etsy; needs reportlab or pypdf (not installed).

name: Reverse-engineer other apps with agents (rea) to recreate their features
what: Decompile competitors' apps and rebuild their features
note: Same trap as cloning best-sellers: it copies other people's protected work. rea is MIT and works as described, and installs MCP servers and skills into agent configs on setup; not needed for any rail.

name: AI employees with their own computers, inboxes and phone numbers (Orgo + bops)
what: A team of bots, each on a cloud desktop with its own email and phone, running business ops
note: Needs agent-created accounts (killed with X3), a Mac app, an OpenAI key and an Orgo account, and the licence is FSL-1.1. We keep its good patterns: approval-gated writes, standing watches, per-agent least privilege, shared memory.

metric: cost per image; share of images served free
kill: a quality drop the QA gates catch on more than 10% of stills
note: Supersedes the Cloudflare Workers Paid idea: at our volume the $5 base fee makes it dearer than Muapi. Plan cost about $5.94 a month at 5 videos a day; the wallet covers about 107 days. Same FLUX.2 klein 4B family as the free tier, 720x1280.
name: Image supply: Muapi FLUX.2 klein behind the free Cloudflare budget
what: When the free 10,000 neurons a day run out, images come from Muapi at $0.0052 each (hook still $0.0104) instead of OpenRouter at $0.04
built: faceless/providers/images.py muapi() in the chain after cloudflare, with a daily USD cap, in-flight reservation, credit-exhaustion block and NSFW rejection; forecast and doctor show the wallet

metric: average view duration and swipe-away rate on clip vs still hooks
note: Live test 2026-10-08: seedance-pro-i2v-fast, 5.04 s, 720x1280, frames showed a faithful push-in with no warping, $0.15, 83 s. Ships OFF because it is new recurring spend; at max 2 a day it is about $0.30 a day. Also addresses YouTube's slideshow/templated-content rule by putting real motion in the opening.
name: Animated hook clips from the hook still (Muapi image-to-video)
what: The first shot becomes a real slow camera move, made automatically for about $0.15, frames QA-checked before use; the owner's Flow clips still win when waiting
built: faceless/hookclip.py + qa.check_frames, wired into visuals behind [production.hookclip]

name: Second-language editions: the same videos in Spanish and Portuguese
what: Each finished video re-voiced with a free Edge neural voice (es-MX, es-US, pt-BR exist, checked 2026-10-08), script translated by the LLM chain, captions re-timed, same stills
metric: views per video in the new language vs English at the same age; hold rate under the translated gauntlet
kill: under 30% of English views after 20 videos, or a policy flag for reused content
note: Multiplies output with no new visuals. Risks: translation quality (needs a native-speaker spot check), the gauntlet's English-only gates (claims, hype, number format), and platform rules on re-uploads, so each language is its own channel. Idea from the ElevenLabs dubbing skill; no ElevenLabs spend needed.

name: Better sound effects: swap the synthesized cut hits for a one-time library of generated whooshes and pops
what: The renderer already mixes a synthesized hit at every cut (music.sfx_track). This would replace those with about twelve generated, real-sounding hits stored in assets/sfx, same level, same loudness target
metric: average view duration, SFX videos vs without
kill: listening test says the synthesized hits are fine, or any loudness-gate failure
note: A polish idea only. Build it if you listen to a finished video and the cut sounds feel cheap; otherwise leave the synthesized layer alone.

name: Demand-ranked topics: TokConnect and Muapi data feed the backlog, production picks high scores first
what: The weekly research session records demand evidence on backlog ideas; next_topic picks the highest score first
capital: 10 TokConnect credits a week (48 free left)
metric: median views of demand-scored topics vs unscored, after 40 videos
note: Built 2026-10-08: ideate.demand_score and the faceless-trends skill. The first lookups found content gaps (budget with me, adhd budgeting, budget setup). vidIQ would add YouTube Shorts data if you connect it.

name: Mistral as a fourth script provider (resilience)
what: An OpenAI-compatible provider behind Gemini, LongCat and OpenRouter, using the Mistral key already in the environment
capital: $0 on the free tier (check the plan before relying on it)
metric: days a script was written by the fallback instead of failing
note: Not built: using the key needs your yes. The key is named MINSTRAL_API_KEY (a typo); the provider would read both spellings.

name: Site analytics with PostHog: visits, calculator use and clicks to the shop
what: Measures the part of the funnel we are blind to: video to site to product page
metric: share of visits that reach a listing link
kill: under 100 visits a week after 8 weeks
note: A PostHog key is in the environment. The snippet must respect consent rules for visitors in the EU and UK (cookie-less mode), so it ships with a privacy line on the site.

name: Etsy draft rail: create DRAFT listings through the Etsy API, never publish
what: A thin draft-only client (create listing, upload images, upload the digital file) mirroring shop.py's Gumroad rail
metric: minutes saved per listing vs the checklist (about 15)
kill: Etsy flags the shop, or the app is refused
note: Parked on purpose: a brand-new shop whose first listings arrive by API looks automated, and the ready packs make the manual route 15 minutes each. Reconsider once the shop has sales history. Reference: etspi-cli (GPL-3.0, use as a separate tool only).

name: Timely macro facts for scripts: US Treasury (keyless) and FRED
what: Dated, sourced numbers (national debt, Treasury rates; inflation and mortgage rates with a FRED key) added to the fact sheet
metric: share of math-pillar scripts citing a dated source; zero fact-check failures
kill: the numbers do not lift saves or shares after 30 videos
note: Checked 2026-10-08 from our network: Treasury FiscalData works keyless; FRED timed out and the BLS public API had its shared daily quota used. A free FRED key (or another egress) is the unlock. Every number must carry its as-of date.
